question:
A group of students studies special square matrices by comparing each matrix with its transpose. They are given $S=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\-1&4&0\\3&0&5\end{bmatrix}$ and $K=\begin{bmatrix}0&2&-4\\-2&0&3\\4&-3&0\end{bmatrix}$. They are also told that $P=\begin{bmatrix}4&x&2\\3&5&-1\\2&-1&6\end{bmatrix}$ is symmetric. Finally, another matrix $Q=[q_{ij}]$ of order 3 is known to be skew-symmetric with $q_{12}=4$, $q_{13}=-2$ and $q_{23}=5$. The students must use the defining relations between a matrix and its transpose to examine and complete these matrices.

(a) Find $S^T$ and determine whether $S$ is symmetric.

(b) Find $K^T$ and determine whether $K$ is skew-symmetric.

(c) Determine the value of $x$ so that $P$ is symmetric.

(d) Construct the complete matrix $Q$ using the given entries and the condition that $Q$ is skew-symmetric.
explanation:
(a)
Transposing $S$ gives $S^T=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\-1&4&0\\3&0&5\end{bmatrix}$. Thus, $S^T=S$. A square matrix satisfying $S^T=S$ is symmetric. Hence, $S$ is a symmetric matrix.

(b)
Transposing $K$ gives $K^T=\begin{bmatrix}0&-2&4\\2&0&-3\\-4&3&0\end{bmatrix}$. Also, $-K=\begin{bmatrix}0&-2&4\\2&0&-3\\-4&3&0\end{bmatrix}$. Therefore, $K^T=-K$. Hence, $K$ is a skew-symmetric matrix.

(c)
For a symmetric matrix, entries placed symmetrically about the principal diagonal must be equal. In $P$, the entries in positions $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$ are $x$ and 3 respectively. Therefore, $x=3$. The other corresponding pairs already agree, so $P$ is symmetric when $x=3$.

(d)
For a skew-symmetric matrix, $q_{ji}=-q_{ij}$ and each diagonal entry is zero. Therefore, $q_{21}=-4$, $q_{31}=2$ and $q_{32}=-5$, while $q_{11}=q_{22}=q_{33}=0$. Hence, $Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&4&-2\\-4&0&5\\2&-5&0\end{bmatrix}$. Its transpose is $Q^T=\begin{bmatrix}0&-4&2\\4&0&-5\\-2&5&0\end{bmatrix}=-Q$, verifying that the constructed matrix is skew-symmetric.

options.A:
(a) $S^T=S$, so $S$ is symmetric.
(b) $K^T=-K$, so $K$ is skew-symmetric.
(c) $x=-3$.
(d) $Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&4&-2\\-4&0&5\\2&-5&0\end{bmatrix}$.
options.B:
(a) $S^T=S$, so $S$ is symmetric.
(b) $K^T=K$, so $K$ is symmetric.
(c) $x=3$.
(d) $Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&4&-2\\4&0&5\\-2&5&0\end{bmatrix}$.
options.C:
(a) $S^T=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\-1&4&0\\3&0&5\end{bmatrix}=S$, so $S$ is symmetric.
(b) $K^T=\begin{bmatrix}0&-2&4\\2&0&-3\\-4&3&0\end{bmatrix}=-K$, so $K$ is skew-symmetric.
(c) $x=3$.
(d) $Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&4&-2\\-4&0&5\\2&-5&0\end{bmatrix}$.
options.D:
(a) $S^T=-S$, so $S$ is skew-symmetric.
(b) $K^T=-K$, so $K$ is skew-symmetric.
(c) $x=3$.
(d) $Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&4&-2\\-4&0&-5\\2&5&0\end{bmatrix}$.
